A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SID research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures and renumbered appendix analyses.

before.justification: v2 reports original SID experiments across multiple LVLMs, including hallucination benchmarks, general-capability evaluations, efficiency measurements, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds reasoning-benchmark evaluations, additional baseline comparisons, and supplementary analyses in Appendices A.5–A.7.

M1.justification: Both versions use CT2S to preserve low-attention vision tokens after early decoder layers and contrast the resulting logits. The scoring rule, decoding equations, and default layer/pruning settings remain unchanged. Applying SID alongside LURE and HA-DPO does not document an alteration to SID itself.

E1.justification: v3 adds MathVista, MMVet, and MMMU, extending evaluation to visual mathematics, integrated multimodal capabilities, and multidisciplinary knowledge and reasoning. LLaVA-Bench-in-the-Wild, previously used for qualitative captioning cases, also receives a formal question-answering evaluation in Appendix A.5 and Table 8.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated comparisons with LURE and HA-DPO in Table 10, AVISC in Table 13, and VDGD in Table 15. LURE and HA-DPO were previously cited but not experimentally compared; v3 also evaluates their combinations with SID and VCD. Existing main-text comparators remain.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce MathVista test-mini, the 24-image/60-question LLaVA-Bench evaluation, and MMVet's LLM-based scoring. Table 10 adds MiniGPT-4 13B and comparisons combining decoding with auxiliary-network or instruction-tuned systems under greedy decoding. These expand the evaluation design; existing CHAIR/POPE protocols and SID defaults are retained.

E4.justification: v3 extends the plausibility-constraint ablation from POPE to CHAIR and MME in Table 11, tests SID's complementarity with LURE and HA-DPO in Table 10, and adds object/attribute MME breakdowns in Table 9. Earlier layer, pruning, hyperparameter, larger-backbone, and sampling-strategy analyses remain.

E5.justification: Table 5 gains uncertainty values using ± notation, and new Table 11 explicitly reports averages over three runs with three random seeds. v2 already included three-run averages and ± reporting elsewhere. v3 does not define Table 5's uncertainty statistic, and the PDFs do not establish an increase in run counts.

E6.justification: New Tables 8–11 and 15, plus AVISC rows in Table 13, substantially expand reported findings. Most existing results are retained, but Table 5 revises SID's MME score from 1520.2 to 1520.4 and MMBench from 65.1 to 65.0. New Table 15 reports VDGD above SID on MMBench, 65.2 versus 65.0, while SID performs better on its hallucination metrics.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same substantive definitions and reasoning, including contrastive decoding, plausibility constraints, attention scoring, the visual-enhancement alternative, and CHAIR metrics. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: contextual token-level hallucination amplification and subtraction, improved faithfulness while preserving general ability, and reduced contrastive-decoding cost. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly discusses residual fine-detail hallucinations in the existing case studies and tentatively attributes them to visual-encoder limitations in Appendix A.6. It also explains InstructBLIP's visualization limitation and adds interpretations of AVISC and VDGD behavior. The main explanation of SID remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 provides VDGD's detailed prompt and reimplementation description, identifies backbones for the new LURE/HA-DPO comparisons, and clarifies that Table 6 measures whole-dataset inference time. The anonymous code pointer is removed, while the GitHub address already present in v2 is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning against AVISC and VDGD, citations for new benchmarks and potential auxiliary detectors, and background references on multimodal learning, federation, and trustworthiness. The main related-work taxonomy and novelty claim remain stable. The Zhao citation's year change refers to the same work.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained. Changes include localized wording corrections, author and affiliation updates, acknowledgements, expanded discussion and future work, and a new Appendix A.5 that shifts the subsequent appendix numbering.

P2.justification: v3 adds five appendix tables and expands v2 Table 9 into v3 Table 13. Table 5 is reformatted for uncertainty reporting, table captions generally move above their tables, and appendix prompts and cases are packed into shared pages. Figures 1–15 are retained with relocation, resizing, and small label corrections.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens an already extensive evaluation with reasoning benchmarks, broader competitors, and additional constraint and compatibility tests. Its discussion of remaining hallucinations also improves balance. Reporting remains imperfect: Table 5's ± values are undefined, and Tables 5 and 10 give unexplained different SID MME scores, 1520.4 and 1525.3. The additions provide a useful but qualified overall improvement.
